s: Ability to distinguish two closely placed objects is
x: Resolving power is the ability of an instrument to distinguish two closely placed objects as separate.

s: Which of these travels in glass with minimum velocity?
x: Violet light has the highest refractive index in glass, so it travels with the minimum velocity (v = c/n). Red travels fastest.

s: Which of the following is not a unit of speed?
x: Speed has the dimension of length/time. m²/hr is area per time, so it is not a unit of speed.

s: For a body moving with uniform acceleration its final velocity equals ........... .
x: For uniform acceleration, average velocity = (u+v)/2, so v = 2 × average velocity − u.

s: The first equation of motion gives the relation between
x: The first equation of motion, v = u + at, relates velocity and time.

s: The second equation of motion gives the relation between
x: The second equation of motion, s = ut + ½at², relates position (displacement) and time.

s: The rate of change of displacement with time is called as ...... .
x: Velocity is defined as the rate of change of displacement with time.

s: In a vacuum, a five-rupee coin a, feather of sparrow bird and a mango are dropped simultaneously from the same height. The time taken by them to reach the bottom is t1, t 2 and t 3 , respectively. In this situation, we will observe that
x: In a vacuum there is no air resistance, so all bodies fall with the same acceleration g irrespective of mass. Hence t1 = t2 = t3.

s: The bond which is present between water molecules is
x: Water molecules are held together by hydrogen bonds between the H of one molecule and the O of another; this is why water has a high boiling point.

s: Where does Amoeba digests its food ?
x: Amoeba engulfs food with pseudopodia into a food vacuole, where digestive enzymes digest it.

s: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) looks rough under the microscope because of the attachment of which one of following cell organelles to its surface?
x: Ribosomes attached to the surface of the endoplasmic reticulum give it a rough appearance (RER), where they make proteins.

s: Flower in which pollination takes place through insect, their pollen grains are
x: Insect-pollinated flowers have rough, sticky pollen grains that cling to insect bodies, while wind-pollinated pollen is smooth, light and dry.

s: Which one of the following pairs of animals is warm blooded ?
x: Birds (peacock) and mammals (camel) are warm-blooded. Crocodile, tortoise (reptiles) and hagfish and dogfish (fishes) are cold-blooded.

s: To study meiosis in plants, the best part would be
x: Meiosis occurs in the cells that form gametes; in plants, pollen mother cells in the anthers undergo meiosis. Shoot, root and leaf cells divide by mitosis.

s: At magnetic poles, the angle of dip is
x: The angle of dip is 0° at the magnetic equator and 90° at the magnetic poles, where the field is vertical.

s: In artificial insemination process, which of the following is/are introduced into the uterus of the female?
x: In artificial insemination, collected semen (sperm) is introduced into the female's uterus, and fertilisation happens inside the body.

s: The temperature which has the same reading on both Fahrenheit and Celsius scales is
x: Setting F = C in F = 9C/5 + 32 gives C = -40, so -40° is the same on both scales.

s: A man weighing 70 kg is coming down in lift. It the cable of the lift breaks sudden, the weight of the man would become
x: When the cable breaks, the lift and the man are in free fall, so the apparent weight (normal reaction) becomes zero.

s: The unit of pressure is
o: None of the above/More than one of the above

s: Pressure is a scalar quantity because
o: it is the ratio of force to area and both force and area are vectors.
it is the ratio of magnitude of force to area.
it is the ratio of component of force (normal to area) to area
x: Pressure is a scalar because it is the ratio of the normal component of force to area, and it has no direction.

s: One nanometer is equal to ……… meters.
x: The prefix nano means 10^-9, so 1 nanometre = 10^-9 m.

s: Intercalary meristems are found in
x: Intercalary meristems lie at the base of leaves or internodes (as in grasses) and help increase length; so they are found in the internode.

s: Magnetic keepers are used to protect magnets from
x: Soft iron keepers placed across the poles of stored magnets complete the magnetic circuit and prevent self-demagnetisation caused by the poles' own opposing fields.

s: Which one of the following is mono- atomic ?
x: Helium, a noble gas, exists as single atoms (monoatomic). Hydrogen is diatomic, sulphur is S8 and phosphorus is P4.

s: The proposition ‘equal volumes of different gases contain equal numbers of molecules at the same temperature and pressure’ is known as
x: Avogadro's hypothesis states that equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

s: Ice is packed in saw dust because
o: saw dust will not get melted easily.
saw dust is poor conductor of heat.
saw dust is a good conductor of heat.
saw dust does not stick to the ice.
x: Sawdust is a poor conductor of heat, so it insulates the ice from outside heat and slows melting.

s: According to the Second Law of Motion, for a given force, acceleration is inversely proportional to the ……… of an object.
x: By Newton's second law, a = F/m, so for a given force acceleration is inversely proportional to mass.

s: Acceleration due to gravity of planet decreases with ..... .
o: decrease in radius of the planet
increase in mass of the planet
decrease in mass of the body
increase in altitude from surface of the planet
x: g = GM/r^2, so g decreases as the distance from the planet's centre increases, i.e. with altitude. g increases with the planet's mass and is independent of the body's mass.

s: Most of photosynthesis process occur in
o: blue and red region of light.
in the green and yellow region of light.
in the blue and orange region of light.
in the violet and orange region of light.
x: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly blue and red light, so photosynthesis is highest there; green light is mostly reflected.

s: A liquid disturbed by stirring comes to rest due to
x: Viscosity is the internal friction of a fluid that opposes relative motion between its layers, so a stirred liquid gradually comes to rest.

s: The density of water is 1 g./cc. This is strictly valid at
x: Water has its maximum density of 1 g/cc at 4°C; at other temperatures such as 0°C or 100°C it is slightly lower.

s: Which of the following is not a noble gas?
x: Neon, helium and argon are Group 18 noble gases; hydrogen is a reactive Group 1 element, so it is not a noble gas.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Annual rings are distinct in plants which grow in temperate region.

II. growing rings of plant is consist of spring wood and autumn wood.
Which of the statements given above is/ are correct about annual ring?
x: In temperate regions seasons alternate, so distinct annual rings form, each made of spring (early) wood and autumn (late) wood. Both statements are correct.

s: Which of the following plants is carnivorous ?
x: Venus flytrap traps and digests insects, so it is carnivorous; the other plants are not insectivorous.

s: Rocket works on the principle of
Which of the following statements regarding magnetic field is not correct?
o: Magnetic field is a quantity that has direction and magnitude.
magnetic field lines are closed curves.
Magnetic field lines are open curves.
No two magnetic field lines are found to cross each other.
x: Magnetic field lines are continuous closed curves (they continue inside the magnet), so saying they are open curves is incorrect.

s: Which one of the following is not a luminous object?
x: Luminous objects emit their own light; the Moon only reflects sunlight, so it is not luminous.

s: A positively charged particle projected towards West is deflected towards North by a magnetic field. What is the direction of magnetic field?
x: By Fleming's left-hand rule, F = qv × B. With v toward West and force toward North, B must point upward.

s: What is the term of the space around a magnet where its influence can be detected?
x: The region around a magnet where its influence can be detected is called its magnetic field.

s: The centre of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called the
x: The centre of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called its pole; the centre of curvature and focus lie off the surface.

s: The spring constant of a spring depends on its
o: thickness, its diameter and its material
x: A spring's constant depends on its material, wire thickness, coil diameter and length, so option 4 is the best answer, not a single factor.

s: Which one of the following statement about magnetic field lines is not correct?
o: They can emanate from a point.
They do not cross each other.
Field lines between two poles cannot be precisely straight lines at the ends.
There are no field lines within a bar magnet.

s: When an object is kept between two parallel plane mirrors then what is the number of images formed?
x: Between two parallel plane mirrors, images keep reflecting back and forth, producing an infinite number of images.

s: During ............. motion of an object along a straight line, the change in velocity of the object for any time interval is zero.
x: In uniform motion, velocity is constant, so the change in velocity over any time interval is zero.

s: If the distance-time graph is a curve then it represents ........... .
x: A curved distance-time graph has a changing slope, meaning the speed changes, which is non-uniform speed.

s: The apparent weight of man in a lift is less the real weight when
o: the lift is going up with an acceleration.
the lift is going down with uniform speed.
the lift is going up with uniform speed.
the lift is going down with an acceleration.
x: When the lift accelerates downward, apparent weight is m(g-a), which is less than mg. At uniform speed apparent weight equals real weight.

s: The moment of inertia of a body does not depend upon its
A solid disc and a solid sphere have the same mass and same radius. Which one has the higher moment of inertia about its centre of mass?
o: Both have the same moment of inertia.
The information provided is not sufficient to answer the question.
x: For the same mass and radius, a solid disc has I = ½MR², while a solid sphere has I = 2/5MR². ½ is larger than 2/5, so the disc has the higher moment of inertia.

s: The period of a simple pendulum is doubled, when
o: the Mass of the bob is doubled.
its length is made four times.
The Mass of the bob and the length of the pendulum are doubled.
x: The period T = 2π√(L/g) is independent of mass and proportional to √L, so making the length four times doubles the period.

s: Which one of the following is not a contact force?
x: Gravitational force acts at a distance without contact, whereas push, friction and strain forces need contact.

s: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion. Which one of the following statements about the acceleration of the oscillating particle is true?
o: It is always in the opposite direction to velocity.
It is proportional to the frequency of oscillation.
It is minimum when the speed is maximum.
It decreases as the potential energy increases.
x: In SHM, acceleration is proportional to displacement, so it is zero at the mean position where speed is maximum. The notes do not cover this.

s: When the milk is churned vigorously the cream from it is separated out due to
x: Churning or cream separation uses centrifugal action, as in centrifugation: the denser skim milk is flung outward and the lighter cream stays near the axis.

s: A brick is thrown vertically from an aircraft flying 2 km above the earth. The brick will fall with a
o: constant speed for some time then with constant acceleration as it means the earth.
x: After release the brick is under gravity alone, so it has constant acceleration g (ignoring air resistance). Its speed and velocity keep changing.

s: The distance-time graph for the motion of an object moving with a constant speed is a
x: With constant speed, distance is proportional to time, so the distance-time graph is a straight line.

s: If the distance between the earth and the sun were twice what it is now, the gravitational force exerted on the earth by the sun would be
o: twice as large as it is now.
four times as large as it is now.
one-fourth of what it is now.
Half of what it is now.
x: Gravitational force follows the inverse-square law, F ∝ 1/r². Doubling the distance makes the force one-fourth.

s: In which of the following places is the acceleration due to gravity zero?
o: At the centre of the earth
x: Inside the earth g decreases linearly with depth and becomes zero at the centre. At the poles, the equator and sea level it is non-zero.

s: To change a temperature from the Kelvin scale to the Celsius scale, you have to
x: Celsius = Kelvin − 273, so you subtract 273 from the Kelvin value.

s: Due to atmospheric refraction, sunrise in advanced and sunset is delayed by about
x: Atmospheric refraction lets us see the sun about 2 minutes before it actually rises and after it actually sets.

s: A bomb explodes on the moon. You will heard its sound on earth after ………
o: you cannot hear the sound of explosion
x: Sound needs a material medium. Space between the moon and earth is a vacuum, so no sound reaches earth.

s: Crossing over occurs during meiosis at
x: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes occurs in the pachytene substage of prophase I.

s: To open a door easily, the handle should be fixed
o: away from mid-point opposite to hinges
x: Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the hinge. A handle far from the hinges gives a larger torque for the same force.

s: What is the direction of magnetic field lines in a magnet?
x: Outside a magnet, field lines run from the north pole to the south pole (they close inside from S to N).

s: Which of the following statements is true? The velocity of sound is
o: less in summer than in winter.
more in summer than in winter.
x: Sound travels faster in warmer air, since speed rises with temperature. So it is faster in summer than in winter.

s: In a periscope, the two plane mirrors are kept
o: at an angle of 60° with each other.
at an angle of 45° with each other.
x: A periscope has two plane mirrors parallel to each other, each inclined at 45° to the tube. This makes the emergent ray parallel to the incident ray.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct about the magnification of an optical microscope?
o: Magnification increases with the increase in focal length of eyepiece.
Magnification increases with the increase in focal length of objective.
Magnification does not depend upon the focal length of eyepiece.
Magnification decreases with the increase in focal length of eyepiece.
x: Microscope magnification is roughly (L/fo)(D/fe), so it falls as the eyepiece focal length rises.

s: What is the definition for the term ‘hibernation’ ?
o: A state of hyperactivity in spring time among birds.
Building of habitat (nests) by birds to save themselves in rainy season.
A state of reduced metabolic activity during winter season among some animals.
A habit of food conservation during summer season for winter among animals.
x: Hibernation is winter dormancy in which some animals have greatly reduced metabolic activity.

s: The working principle of a mercury thermometer is
o: change in density of matter on heating.
change in mass of matter on heating.
x: A mercury thermometer works on the expansion of mercury on heating.

s:
Which of the following angles are equal in case of plane mirror?

I. Angle of incidence

II. Angle of refraction

III. Angle of reflection
o: All the given angles are equal
x: A plane mirror reflects light and does not refract it. By the law of reflection the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

s: The SI unit for the average velocity is ……… .
x: Velocity is displacement divided by time, so its SI unit is m/s. m/s² is the unit of acceleration.

s: Light waves are ……… .
x: Light is an electromagnetic wave, made of oscillating electric and magnetic fields.

s: Which of the following quantities does not have any unit?
x: Relative density is the ratio of two densities (substance to water), so the units cancel and it has no unit, whereas speed, density and acceleration all have units.

s: Electromagnet is constructed with which of the following?
x: An electromagnet needs a core that magnetises strongly and loses magnetism quickly when current stops; soft iron does this, while steel retains magnetism.

s: Iron sheet kept in moist air covered with rust. Rust is
o: a mixture of iron and dust
a mixture of iron, oxygen and water
x: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3.xH2O, a chemical compound with fixed composition formed by a chemical reaction, not a mixture.

s: Constantan is an alloy of copper and ......
x: Constantan is an alloy of about 60% copper and 40% nickel, used in resistance wires and thermocouples.

s: Which one of the following compounds does not exhibt a different oxidation number of the same element?
x: In Fe2O3 iron is +3 throughout. Pb3O4 (Pb +2/+4), Fe3O4 (Fe +2/+3) and Mn3O4 (Mn +2/+3) each have the same element in two oxidation states.

s: Multiplication of equivalent weight and valency of an element is equal to …… .
x: Atomic weight = equivalent weight × valency, which is the standard relation.

s: The rusting of iron nail
o: does not affect weight but iron is oxidised.
does not affect weight but iron is reduced.
x: Rusting is oxidation of iron, which combines with oxygen and water to form hydrated oxide, so the nail's weight increases.

s:
Which of the following statements are correct?

I. Change in magnetic field produces induced current.

II. Flow of current in a conductor produces magnetic field.

III. Magnetic field related to coil can be produced by motion between conductor and coil.
x: All three statements are correct: a changing magnetic field induces current (Faraday), a current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field (Oersted), and relative motion between conductor and coil changes the flux and so produces induction.

s: A metal plate with a circular hole at the centre is heated. What will happen to the area of the hole?
o: Will increase first and then decrease
x: On heating, a plate expands uniformly, including the hole, which behaves as if it were made of the same material, so the hole's area increases.

s: Integrated circuits are made up of which of the following?
x: Integrated circuits are fabricated on silicon, a semiconductor, wafers.

s: Which one of the following will not produce carbon dioxide on reacting with an aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid?
x: Limestone, chalk and marble are all calcium carbonate, which releases CO2 with HCl. Quicklime (CaO) is an oxide and gives only CaCl2 and water.

s: Inert gases are
x: Inert (noble) gases have complete outer electron shells, so they are chemically unreactive and stable.

s: Which one of the following is not a semiconductor?
x: Silicon, germanium and gallium arsenide are semiconductors; quartz (SiO2) is an insulator.

s: When a piece of pure silicon is doped with aluminium, then
o: the conductivity of the doped silicon piece will remain the same.
the doped silicon piece will become n-type.
the doped silicon piece will become p-type.
the resistivity of the doped silicon piece will increase.
x: Aluminium is trivalent, an acceptor impurity in tetravalent silicon, which creates holes and makes it p-type.

s: If there were no gravity, which of the following will not be there for a fluid?
x: Upthrust (buoyancy) arises from pressure differences caused by the fluid's weight under gravity, so it disappears without gravity. Viscosity and surface tension are molecular forces and remain.

s: Soap bubble attains spherical shape due to ……… .
x: Surface tension makes a liquid surface contract to minimum area, and a sphere has the least surface area for a given volume, so a soap bubble is spherical.

s: Which one of the following statement(s) is/are not correct?
o: The response of the ear to sound of increasing intensity is approximately logarithmic.
The sensitivity of the human ear does not vary with the frequency of the sound.
When two or more waves traverse the same medium, the displacement of any element of the medium is the algebraic sum of the displacements due to each wave.
Longitudinal waves can travel in all media; solids, liquids and gases.
x: Human ear sensitivity varies strongly with frequency (most sensitive about 2-5 kHz), so statement 2 is incorrect.

s: Action and reaction …..… .
x: By Newton's third law, action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, acting on different bodies.

s:
A brass ball is tied to a thin wire and swung so as to move uniformly in a horizontal circle.
Which of the following statements in this regard is/are ture?

I. The ball moves with constant velocity.

II. The ball moves with constant speed.

III. The ball moves with constant acceleration.

IV. The magnitude of the acceleration of the ball is constant.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
x: In uniform circular motion speed is constant but the velocity direction changes. The acceleration is centripetal with constant magnitude but changing direction, so only II and IV are true.

s:
Consider the following reaction. CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2 O
Which of the following about the reaction given above is/are correct?

I. Carbon is oxidised

II. Hydrogen is oxidised

III. Hydrogen is reduced

IV. Carbon is reduced
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: In CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O only carbon is oxidised (−4 to +4), while hydrogen stays at +1 and oxygen is reduced.

s:
Consider the following cell organelles of the organisms.

I. Mitochondria

II. Chloroplasts

III. Endoplasmic Reticulum
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are semi-autonomous organelle(s)?
x: Mitochondria and chloroplasts contain their own DNA and ribosomes and make some of their own proteins, so they are semi-autonomous. The endoplasmic reticulum has no DNA, so it is not.

s: Which one of the following statements about sound is not correct?
o: Sound travels at a speed slower than the speed of light.
Sound travels faster in moist air than in dry air.
x: Sound waves are longitudinal (compressions and rarefactions), not transverse, so the statement that they are transverse is the incorrect one.

s: Ultra purification of a metal is done by :
x: Zone melting is the method used to obtain ultra-pure metals such as germanium and silicon. Slugging, smelting and leaching are not ultra-purification methods.

s: In simple harmonic motion, acceleration is at
x: In SHM, a = -ω²x, so the magnitude of acceleration is greatest at the extreme positions (amplitude) and zero at equilibrium.

s: Quality of a musical note depends on
o: velocity of sound in the medium.
x: Quality (timbre) of a musical note depends on the harmonics (overtones) present. Pitch depends on frequency and loudness on amplitude.

s:
Which of the following is an example of unicellular organism ?

I. Euglena
II. Amoeba

III. Paramecium
x: Euglena, Amoeba and Paramecium are all single-celled organisms, so all the options listed are correct.

s:
Consider the following statement. If there were no phenomenon of capillarity, then

I. It would be difficult to use a kerosene lamp.

II. One would not be able to use a straw to consume a soft drink.

III. The blotting paper would fail to function.

IV. The big trees that we see around would not have grown on the earth.
Which of the following statements given above are correct?
o: I, II, III and IV only
x: Capillarity lets oil rise in a lamp wick, ink be absorbed by blotting paper, and water reach the tops of tall trees. A straw works by suction (air pressure), not capillarity, so II is wrong.

s: Waves produced at the bottom of the sea due to an explosion are… .
x: Sound-type pressure waves from an underwater explosion travel through the water as longitudinal waves, because a fluid cannot support transverse waves.

s:
Which of the following are the characteristics of electromagnetic waves?

I. They are elastic waves.

II. They can also move in vacuum.

III. They have electric and magnetic components which are mutually perpendicular.

IV. They move with a speed equal to 3 lakh meters per second.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: EM waves are non-elastic, travel in vacuum, and have mutually perpendicular E and B fields. Their speed is 3×10^8 m/s (3 lakh km/s), not 3 lakh m/s, so IV is wrong.

s:
Which of the following occurs due to refraction?

I. The apparent displacement of a pencil, partly immersed in water.

II. Sun appears before the sunrise.

III. Sky appears blue.
x: The apparent bending of a pencil in water and the sun appearing before sunrise are refraction effects. The blue sky is due to scattering, not refraction.

s:
In case of a compound microscope, which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. The focal length of the eyepiece is larger than the focal length of the objective.

II. The focal length of the eyepiece is smaller than the focal length of the objective.

III. The image produced in a normal optical microscope is real.

IV. The image produced in a normal optical microscope is virtual.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
x: In a compound microscope the eyepiece has a longer focal length than the objective. The final image seen is virtual, inverted and magnified.

s:
Which of the following are the properties of an electron?

I. Electron is a constituent of cathode ray.

II. Electron is a negatively charged particle.

III. The mass of the electron is equal to the mass of the proton.

IV. Electron is deflected by the electric field but not by magnetic field.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The electron is a negatively charged constituent of cathode rays. Its mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, and it is deflected by both electric and magnetic fields.

s:
Which of the following solutions will not change the colour of blue litmus paper to red?

I. Acid solution

II. Base solution

III. Common salt solution
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Only acids turn blue litmus red. Base and neutral salt solutions do not, so II and III are the answer.

s:
Which of the following is/are state function/functions ?

I. q + W
II. q
III.W
IV. H − TS
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: q + W gives the change in internal energy, a state function, and H - TS is the Gibbs free energy, also a state function. q and W individually are path functions.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?

I. Viruses lack enzymes necessary for the generation of energy.

II. Viruses can be cultured in any synthetic medium.

III. Viruses are transmitted from one organism to another by biological vectors only.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Viruses lack the enzymes for energy generation. They cannot be cultured in synthetic media because they need living host cells, and they are not transmitted only by biological vectors.

s:
Consider the following fuction of xylem.

I. Conduction of water

II. Conduction of minerals.

III. Mechanical support.
Which of the function (s) of xylem given above is/are correct?
x: Xylem conducts water and minerals and also gives mechanical support through its fibres, so all three are correct.

s:
Which of the following statements about DNA is/are correct?

I. DNA is the hereditary material of all living organisms.

II. All segments of DNA code for synthesis of proteins.

III. Nuclear DNA is double helical with two nucleotide chains which run anti-parallel.

IV. DNA is also found in mitochondria.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: DNA is the hereditary material of most organisms (some viruses use RNA, so I is generally accepted by the key), nuclear DNA is an antiparallel double helix, and mitochondria contain DNA. Not all DNA segments code for proteins, so II is wrong.

s: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror at a point between its centre of curvature and focus. The image will be formed at
o: a point beyond the centre of curvature.
a point between the focus and the centre of curvature.
x: For a concave mirror, an object between C and F gives a real, inverted, magnified image beyond the centre of curvature.

s:
Which of the following statement(s) about specific heat of a body is/are correct?

I. It depends upon mass and shape of the body.

II. It is independent of mass and shape of the body.

III. It depends only upon the temperature of the body.
x: Specific heat is a property of the material. It does not depend on the mass or shape of the body, and it is not dependent only on temperature, so only II is correct.

s:
Which type of image is always formed by a convex mirror?

I. Real
II. Virtual

III. Enlarged
x: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image. Its magnification is less than 1, so it is never enlarged or real.

s:
Which of the following statement(s) about electromagnetic waves, sound waves and water waves is/are correct?

I. They exhibit reflection.

II. They carry energy.

III. They exert pressure.

IV. They can travel in vacuum.
x: Electromagnetic, sound and water waves all reflect, carry energy and exert pressure. Only EM waves travel in vacuum, so statement IV is wrong.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct? The velocity of sound
o: does not depend upon the nature of media.
is maximum in gases and minimum in liquids.
is maximum in solids and minimum in liquids.
is maximum in solids and minimum in gases.
x: Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases, because denser, more elastic media transmit vibrations faster.

s: Role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis is
x: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light energy (mainly red and blue light) to drive photosynthesis. It does not absorb water or CO2.

s: White Phosphorus glows in the dark due to
x: White phosphorus slowly oxidises in air, and this chemiluminescence makes it glow in the dark.

s: A boat full of iron nails is floating on water in a lake. When the iron nails are removed, the water level
x: A floating boat with nails displaces water equal to its total weight. Once the nails are removed and sink, they displace only their own volume, which is less, so the water level falls.

s: The term LASER stand for
o: Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
Light Amplification by Spontaneous Emission of Radiation
Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Rays
Light Amplification by Stimulated Energy of Radiation
x: LASER stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.

s: In which one of the following is the valence electronic configuration, ns2 np 3 found?
x: Nitrogen (Z=7) has configuration 1s2 2s2 2p3, so its valence shell is ns2 np3. Carbon is ns2np2, oxygen ns2np4, argon ns2np6.

s: When pure water boils vigorously, the bubbles that rise to the surface are composed primarily of
x: Boiling is a physical change; the bubbles are water vapour, not air or the gases hydrogen and oxygen.

s: A balloon filled with helium rises in air because
o: air exerts an upward force on the balloon
helium is less dense than air.
helium pushes down on the air below the balloon.
x: Helium is less dense than air, so the buoyant force exceeds the balloon's weight and it rises.

s: The pH of fresh ground water slightly decreases upon exposure to air because
o: carbon dioxide from air is dissolved in the water.
oxygen from air is dissolved in the water.
the dissolved carbon dioxide of the ground water escapes into air.
the dissolved oxygen of the ground water escapes into air.

s: Rust needs three components to occur i.e. .........
x: Rusting is the oxidation of iron in the presence of oxygen and moisture.

s: Which of the following elements is found in all organic compounds?
x: Carbon is the defining element of all organic compounds; others like nitrogen, oxygen and calcium are not universal.

s: Which one of the following gas comes out during photosynthesis?
x: Photosynthesis takes in CO2 and water and releases oxygen.

s: The oxygen evolved during photosynthesis comes from splitting of
x: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from the photolysis (splitting) of water in the light reactions, not from CO2.

s: Which one of the following is not an electromagnetic wave?
x: Sound is a mechanical wave needing a medium, while light, radio waves and microwaves are electromagnetic waves.

s: Which one of the following has the longest wavelength?
x: Among these, infrared has the longest wavelength; the order of increasing wavelength is gamma, UV, visible, infrared.

s: The product of equivalent weight and valency of an element is equal to
x: By the law of equivalents, atomic weight = equivalent weight × valency.

s: Which one of the following properties changes with valency?
x: Equivalent weight = atomic weight / valency, so it changes with valency, while atomic weight, molecular weight and density do not.

s: A car starts from Bengaluru, goes 50 km in a straight line towards South, immediately turns around and returns to Bengaluru. The time taken for this round trip is 2h. The magnitude of the average velocity of the car for this round trip
o: cannot be calculated without knowing acceleration
x: Average velocity is net displacement over time. The car returns to the start, so displacement is zero and so is average velocity.

s: It is easy to burst a gas-filled balloon with a needle than with a nail. It is because
o: nail is more longer than needle.
nail exerts more pressure than needle on the balloon.
needle exerts more pressure than nail on the balloon.
gas is reactive with the needle.
x: Pressure = force/area. The needle's tip has a much smaller area, so for the same force it exerts more pressure and bursts the balloon.

s: The quality or tone of a musical sound produced by a stringed instrument depends on
o: length of the strings in the instrument.
x: Quality (timbre) of a musical sound depends on its wave form, i.e. the mix of harmonics. Pitch depends on frequency and loudness on amplitude.

s: Which of the following is the methods of heat transfer?
x: Convection is one of the three modes of heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation); evaporation, revolution and thermal expansion are not modes of heat transfer.

s: A thermometer is used to measure
x: A thermometer measures temperature, the degree of hotness; heat is energy and is measured by a calorimeter.

s: ……… is not an example of refraction of light.
o: Bending of light while passing through a medium
x: Lateral inversion is caused by reflection in a plane mirror, not refraction. Twinkling, mirages and bending of light in a medium are refraction effects.

s: Which of the following quantities have its SI unit named after Blaise Pascal?
A deep sea diver may hurt his ear drum during diving because of
x: Water pressure increases with depth, so a deep-sea diver's ear drum can be hurt by the high water pressure.

s: Two cars, passing each other at high speed, are in danger of side swiping because
o: of the increase in air pressure in the space between them.
of decrease in the velocity of air molecules between them.
of decrease in air pressure in the space between them.
of the increase in the velocity of air molecules between them.
x: By Bernoulli's principle, fast-moving air between the cars lowers the pressure there. The higher outside pressure pushes the cars together.

s: Under which condition real gas can work as an ideal gas?
x: A real gas behaves ideally at low pressure and high temperature, where molecules are far apart and intermolecular forces are negligible.

s: The SI unit of weight is
x: Weight is a force, so its SI unit is the newton. The kg and gram are units of mass, and the dyne is a CGS unit.

s: Water is used in a hot water bag because
x: Water has a high specific heat, so it stores a large amount of heat and releases it slowly, which makes it suitable for a hot water bag.

s: A liquid is kept in a glass beaker. Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the pressure exerted by the liquid column at the base of the beaker?
o: The pressure depends on the area of the base of the beaker.
The pressure depends on the height of liquid column.
The pressure does not depend on the density of the liquid.
The pressure neither depends on the area of the base of the beaker nor on the height of liquid column.
x: Liquid pressure P = hρg depends on the height of the liquid column and the density, not on the base area.

s: If ice floating on water in a vessel melts, the water level in the vessel …… .
x: Floating ice displaces water equal to its own weight, so the melted ice exactly fills the displaced volume and the level does not change.

s: When water freezes its density
x: Water expands on freezing, so ice has greater volume for the same mass and lower density, which is why ice floats.

s: During the melting of solid, its temperature
o: may increase or decrease depending on the nature of solid.
x: During melting, the heat supplied goes into latent heat to change the state, so the temperature stays constant at the melting point.

s: If the speed of a moving magnet inside a coil increases, the electric current in the coil
x: Electromagnetic induction: a faster-moving magnet changes flux faster, which induces a larger emf and so a larger current.

s: Water is a good solvent. This is due to high
x: Water's high dielectric constant reduces the attraction between ions, so it dissolves ionic substances well.

x: Stomata carry out transpiration, xylem transports water, root hairs absorb water, and phloem transports food, which gives 2 4 1 3.

s: How is the kinetic energy of a moving object affected if the net work done on it is positive?
x: By the work-energy theorem, net work done equals the change in kinetic energy, so positive work increases kinetic energy.

s: The surface tension of water on adding detergent to it
x: Detergent molecules lower the surface tension of water, which helps it wet fabric and remove dirt.

s: Which one of the following is not a result of surface tension?
o: Removal of dirt by soap or detergent
x: Spherical rain drops, capillary rise and detergent cleaning are surface tension effects. The flow of a liquid is related to viscosity, not surface tension.
